data.long_meaning: Derived from the Celtic name Isolde, meaning 'ice-rule' or 'ice-surge'. In Arthurian legend, Yseult was the tragic heroine famed for her beauty and love for Tristan. The name Yseult carries the meaning “Isolde, White Shadow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Yseult usually hope their child will grow to embody isolde, white shadow and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of enduring love and devotion.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yseult total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: יסולט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם יסולט הוא שילוב של המילים העבריות 'יסוד' ו'אל', ומשמעותו היא אלוהים הוא הבסיס והיסוד של אהבה וחסד. השם קשור לשורש העברי 'יסד' שפירושו 'ליסד' או 'להקים', ומציין את האל כמייסד ומקיים של כל דבר.

in_greek.name: Ύσεult
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ύσεult πιθανόν να προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'Ύση', που σημαίνει 'θεραπεία' ή 'σωτηρία', και το επίθετο 'ult', που πιθανόν να σχετίζεται με την έννοια της αγάπης και του ελέους. Το όνομα συνδέεται με την χριστιανική παράδοση και την πνευματική σημασία της αγάπης και του ελέους του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Yseult
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Yseult originem habet in linguis celticis et gallicis, sed in traditione christiana, nomen significat 'Deus est amor et misericordia'. Nomen coniungit ideas amoris et misericordiae Dei, quae sunt aspectus fundamentum spiritualis christiani.

in_english.name: Yseult
in_english.long_meaning: The name Yseult is of Celtic origin, but in Christian tradition, it signifies 'God is love and mercy'. Derived from the roots of 'ys' meaning 'fair' or 'god' and 'eult' meaning 'ultimately' or 'mercy', the name embodies the spiritual significance of God's love and mercy. Historically, the name may be associated with chivalric romances and Christian virtues.
